newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse seen consolidating, watching U.S.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse seen consolidating, watching U.S.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse was expected to take a breather on Friday and consolidate after it it made strides following the results of the U.S. election.
"A bit of a rest would be completely healthy," said one trader. "I expect we'll just move sideways," said another.

The IBIS DAX, which measures day-long computer trade in the DAX index of 30 leading shares, was down 10.76 points, or 0.39 percent, at 2,724.52, by 1537 GMT, but was off the day's lows after German Bunds recovered some ground and Wall Street built on its Wednesday record close.
Wall Street would set the tone for Friday, dealers said.

Dealers said the DAX index was well supported by the technical and psychological level of 2,700 points and would not breach that level on Friday. In bourse trade the DAX had touched a day low of 2,703.96 points, only to rebound to end at 2,713 points.

But some dealers said there was still some nervousness in the market after Siemens surprised the market with a flat outlook for 1996/97, pulling the stock down over eight percent in bourse dealings and dragging the DAX index down.
"First we had the SAP shock and then Siemens. Who knows what could come next?" asked one trader.

Siemens fell nine percent in late Wednesday IBIS dealings after it released its results and forecast, but on Thursday the stock recovered some of its losses to trade up 90 pfennigs at 73.70 in computer dealings.
Meanwhile Daimler came off year highs slipping 40 pfennigs to 93.30, after releasing nine month sales which were mainly in line with expectations.

The chemical sector, on the other hand, was stronger than the market trend, led by Hoechst, which continued to climb after its nine month results, up 16 pfennigs at 60.95 marks, but off an all-time high of 61.65 reached earlier.
Viag AG will be in the spotlight on Friday as it is due to report nine month results early in the morning.
Fresenius Medical Care AG and Fresenius AG will also publish results in the morning.
The release of German August trade figures should also be a talking point.
